question: Do explicit regularized compatibility interactions between Lead Need, Physical Space, Location and Broker improve future prioritization beyond the same profiles used only as marginal effects?
hypothesis: A treatment model with pre-specified compatibility interactions will improve average precision and top-decile lift relative to the same marginal profiles without interactions, especially in Need × Physical Space and Need × Broker combinations.
primary_change: add explicit regularized compatibility interactions to the treatment arm while holding population, target, split and marginal profiles fixed
secondary_changes: evaluate supported future compatibility cells with shrinkage and minimum support
report paired bootstrap uncertainty and lead-level robustness
pre-register a randomized routing A/B protocol using sticky lead-level assignment

target.censoring: The public candidate data has no visit timestamp or true sale. The offline outcome is a proxy; causal lift is reserved for the online randomized experiment.

population.eligibility: Exactly the same eligible inquiries and temporal partitions as E006.
exclusions: Profile calibration rows remain excluded from predictive fitting; A and B use identical train/test rows.

validation.strategy: offline temporal A/B backtest plus pre-registered online randomized A/B design
validation.split_description: Offline A/B: exact same train and untouched future test rows in both arms; only interaction terms differ. Online A/B: 50/50 sticky assignment by lead_id, stratified by search_sector, search_modality and user_type, analyzed by intention-to-treat after the fixed 30-day window.

items.source: derived only from E006 point-in-time-safe profile IDs
items.information_available_at: same as component profiles at inquiry_at
items.evidence: No response outcome, future snapshot or post-inquiry signal is introduced; the treatment differs only by pre-specified crossed categorical terms.
Inherited unchanged from E006 and checked by the same data-quality/leakage gate.
